title: Scaling Agents for Gen AI Products - Anju Kambadur, Bloomberg Head of AI Engineering
talk_summary: Bloomberg's AI engineering lead describes building semi-agentic products where non-optional guardrails and downstream safety checks compensate for fragile, compounding LLM errors. He argues for fast early iteration, then factoring agents and cross-cutting guardrails into smaller, testable pieces with monitoring and circuit breakers.

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat upstream agent/API outputs as fragile and evolving; downstream agents run their own safety checks instead of trusting upstream accuracy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it is easier to not count on the Upstream systems to be accurate but rather factor in that they will be fragile

takeaways.what_they_do: Code guardrails as required checks at multiple points rather than leaving them to agent discretion or autonomy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: those are not optional pieces for any agent those are coded in as you must

takeaways.technique: Downstream task-specific evals for model changes
takeaways.what_they_do: Do not rely on aggregate model improvements; downstream consumers test their own workflows when upstream models/APIs change.
takeaways.evidence_quote: being better means being better on average it doesn't mean it'll be better for you as a downstream consumer

takeaways.what_they_do: Monitor agent outputs and add circuit breakers plus remediation workflows for published or long-running results.
takeaways.evidence_quote: build remediation workflows and circuit breakers

takeaways.what_they_do: Split monolithic agent behavior into smaller agents with clear roles, such as query understanding, retrieval, and answer generation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's factorized as its own agent

takeaways.what_they_do: After early fast iteration, centralize shared concerns like guardrails as horizontal platform pieces rather than duplicating them per team.
